hypothesis: Running the qwen38 engine's layers, routed experts (GPU expert cache) and expert read-ahead on the Metal GPU instead of the CPU makes decode after the 61-token short.txt prompt faster on a 24 GB M4 Pro, with the model's experts streamed from the SSD.
model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next heretic-2, llama.cpp IQ4_XS GGUF (routed experts IQ4_XS gate/up, IQ4_NL down, 2.54 MiB each; trunk mostly Q8_0), imported in link mode (colibri-dev)
command: BUILD='5cc5507e METAL=1' METAL=1 WARMUP=1 PREFILL_RUNS=0 ARM_ENV='USAGE_SAVE=0 COLI_METAL=<0|1>' docs/experiments/qwen38-metal-chain-2026-11-21/q38_bench.sh bench/bin/qwen38-metal-pr ~/models/qwen38-heretic2/colibri-dev pr-<cpu|gpu> 3

hardware.cpu: Apple M4 Pro, 8 performance + 4 efficiency cores (Mac16,8)

config.SNAP: qwen38-heretic2 colibri-dev (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next heretic-2 IQ4_XS GGUF, 5 files, 117 GB, read in place)
config.BUILD: make -C c qwen38 METAL=1 at 5cc5507e, copied to bench/bin/qwen38-metal-pr, one binary for both arms
config.ENGINE: default (fast) kernels; GPU experts on and read-ahead on when the chain runs; default GPU expert cache (6.82 GiB)
config.ENV: SNAP COLI_TEMP=0 Q38_MAXT=32768 USAGE_SAVE=0, OMP_NUM_THREADS unset; argv 32 8 <prompt>
config.PROMPT: q38_bench.sh prompts/short.txt (61 tokens, chat template), 64 greedy tokens
config.ORDER: 1 warm-up run (discarded) then 3 decode runs per arm, CPU arm first, then GPU; one process each; decode only (PREFILL_RUNS=0)
config.MEASURED: decode tok/s = 63 / (decode seconds - TTFT) of each short.txt run
